name: Lies, Lies, Lies

items.name: Play-Doh
items.fact: Play-Doh began as a putty for cleaning soot off wallpaper. When people stopped needing it, the company found that children loved modelling with it and sold it as a toy.

items.name: Listerine
items.fact: Listerine was first made in 1879 as an antiseptic for surgeons. It was later sold as a floor cleaner before becoming a mouthwash.

items.name: Lamborghini
items.fact: Before building sports cars, Ferruccio Lamborghini made tractors. The story goes that he started making cars after he complained to Enzo Ferrari about his own Ferrari's clutch.

items.name: Nokia
items.fact: Nokia started in Finland in 1865 as a paper mill. Over the years it also made rubber boots and car tyres before it became famous for mobile phones.

items.name: Nintendo
items.fact: Nintendo was founded in Kyoto in 1889 to make hanafuda, traditional Japanese playing cards. It didn't make video games until almost a century later.

items.name: Samsung
items.fact: Samsung started in Korea in 1938 as a small trading company selling dried fish, vegetables and noodles. Electronics only came decades later.

items.name: Avon
items.fact: Avon's founder, David McConnell, sold books door to door and gave customers a free bottle of perfume. The perfume was more popular than the books, so he started a perfume company.

items.name: Wrigley's
items.fact: William Wrigley Jr first sold soap, then baking powder, and gave away chewing gum as a free gift. Customers liked the gum more, so he switched to gum.

items.name: Shell
items.fact: The oil company Shell is named after seashells. The founders' father had sold boxes decorated with seashells in London, and the family business grew from there.

items.name: Kellogg's Corn Flakes
items.fact: Corn flakes were first made by the Kellogg brothers as plain health food for patients at a hospital in Michigan. The very first flakes were wheat, from dough that was accidentally left out too long.

fakes.name: The watchmaker's graters
fakes.fact: A Swiss watch brand, Hoffstetter, started in 1871 as a maker of cheese graters. Its first watch cases were cut on the same machines as the graters.

fakes.name: The umbrella shop
fakes.fact: A Korean phone-case maker, Hanbit, began in 1962 by selling paper umbrellas. The founder's son still keeps one of the first umbrellas in the head office.

fakes.name: The espresso engine
fakes.fact: The Italian sports-car maker Ventura Motori began by making espresso machines. Its first car engine was tested in the coffee factory's back room.

fakes.name: The circus saddles
fakes.fact: A German sportswear brand, Kranich, began in 1923 by making leather saddles for circus horses. Its first running shoe used the same leather.

fakes.name: The hospital soap
fakes.fact: The French perfume house Maison Delorme began as a soap factory for hospitals in Lyon. The founder added perfume after nurses complained about the smell.

fakes.name: The silk kites
fakes.fact: The Japanese video-game company Kumori started in 1910 by making silk kites. Its first game, in 1978, was about flying a kite.

fakes.name: The fishing nets
fakes.fact: A Finnish mobile-network company, Verkko, began as a maker of fishing nets in 1890. Its name still means “net” in Finnish.

fakes.name: The dog biscuits
fakes.fact: A British biscuit brand, Pemberton's, started by selling dog biscuits. The founder switched to biscuits for people after his own children kept eating the dogs' ones.

fakes.name: The pram factory
fakes.fact: A Dutch bicycle maker, Van Hulst, began in 1899 as a pram factory. Its first bikes used the same wheels as its prams.

fakes.name: The church candles
fakes.fact: The Spanish chocolate brand Cacao Ribera began by making church candles in Seville. It switched to chocolate when cocoa butter became cheaper than wax.
